answer.reason: 2 Kings 13 tells two events of this Ben-hadad: Israel delivered into his hand, and his defeat by Jehoash.

clauses.english: was given power over Israel when the LORD's anger was kindled against them
clauses.quote: and into the hand of Benhadad the son of Hazael

clauses.english: was beaten three times by Jehoash, who took back the cities of Israel from him
clauses.quote: Three times did Joash beat him

doubts: JER 49:27 and AMO 1:4 foretell fire on the palaces of Benhadad; these are prophecies, not events told of him, and may not mean this Ben-hadad, so they were left out.
2KI 13:24 only says he reigned after Hazael, which the summary already gives.
